newsitem.title: AZERBAIJAN: Chechen leader Maskhadov in Azerbaijan for talks.
newsitem.headline: Chechen leader Maskhadov in Azerbaijan for talks.

text.p: Aslan Maskhadov, leader of Russia's breakaway Chechnya region, arrived on Tuesday for talks with Azeri President Haydar Aliyev on economic issues.
Azerbaijan's presidential press service said Aliyev would meet Maskhadov, who arrived in Baku in a motorcade from the Chechen captial Grozny.
Chechen Vice-President Vakha Arsanov told Reuters by telephone from Grozny that the two men would discuss economic issues and probably the transport of Azeri oil through Chechen territory.
Arsanov said the surprise visit marked the first time Maskhadov had been officially received by a foreign head of state.
Russia, whose troops fought an unsuccessful 21-month war to try to crush the Moslem region's independence bid, still regards Chechnya as its terrritory.
The Chechens say a peace plan they signed keeping them a part of the Russian Federation until 2001 was only to let Moscow save face before eventually letting them secede completely.

Russia and Azerbaijan have had strained relations since the former Soviet republic gained independence in 1991 but, in a sign of a thaw, Aliyev announced last month would pay his first official visit to Moscow on July 3.
Aliyev said he would discuss the transit of oil from Azerbaijan through the pipeline crossing Chechnya to Russia's port at Novorossiisk, due to start by October this year.
Russian Prime Minister Victor Chernomyrdin recently signed an agreement with the Chechen leadership on reparing the Chechen section of the route.
An $8 billion multinational consortium led by British Petroleum plc plans to use the route for early oil transport from three fields it is developing in the Azeri sector of the Caspian Sea.
